rv.q: This production glows with nostalgia swirling around ice cream socials, patriotic pageants, and a lovable con man redeemed by the rubes he wants to con, fashioned with old-fashioned Broadway know-how, and those Willson ballads and marches that we all know by heart.
Andrews plays him too earnestly, and it makes the Act II reveal of his true intentions feel jarring and cruel.
